visibility-intro.title: What is Visibility?
visibility-intro.body:
Visibility measures how easy it is for people AND AI to find your content. It combines two scores:

**SEO Score** — how well search engines (Google, Bing) can index and rank your pages.

**GEO Score** — how likely AI platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) are to cite your content when users ask questions.

A high Visibility score means your content reaches more people through more channels.

actions.a0: Open a document and click the SEO panel to start optimizing
actions.a1: Run Optimize All from the SEO dashboard for a quick boost

geo-score-explained.title: How to improve your GEO score
geo-score-explained.body:
AI platforms prefer content that is structured for citation. The 8 GEO rules check:

1. **Answer-first** — lead with the answer, not background
2. **Question headers** — use H2s that match queries ("How does X work?")
3. **Statistics** — include numbers, percentages, data points
4. **Citations** — reference authoritative external sources
5. **Freshness** — content updated within 90 days
6. **Structured data** — JSON-LD schema configured
7. **Author** — named author for E-E-A-T trust
8. **Content depth** — 800+ words for comprehensive coverage

actions.a0: Use the GEO Optimizer agent to restructure content automatically

seo-meta-fields.title: Why meta title and description matter
seo-meta-fields.body:
Meta title and description control how your page appears in Google search results AND AI citations. Without them, Google guesses — and usually gets it wrong.

**Meta title** — 30-60 characters. Include your primary keyword. This is the blue link in search results.

**Meta description** — 120-160 characters. Compelling summary that makes people click.

**OG image** — the image shown when someone shares your page on social media or messaging apps.

actions.a0: Click AI Optimize on the SEO panel to auto-generate these fields

visibility-fix-issues.title: Fixing missing meta fields
visibility-fix-issues.body:
The Issues count shows documents that lack key SEO/GEO metadata. To fix them quickly:

1. Go to the **Documents** tab below
2. Click any document with missing fields (❌)
3. Open the **SEO panel** in the editor sidebar
4. Click **AI Optimize** to auto-generate title, description, and keywords
5. Review and save

Alternatively, use **Optimize All** on the SEO dashboard to batch-fix everything at once.

actions.a0: Open SEO dashboard for bulk optimization

build-output-files.title: What the build generates for search engines and AI
build-output-files.body:
Every time you build, the CMS automatically generates these discovery files:

**robots.txt** — tells crawlers what they can access (configure strategy in Settings → GEO)

**sitemap.xml** — lists all pages for Google, with hreflang for multi-language sites

**llms.txt** — AI-friendly index of your content structure and MCP endpoint

**llms-full.txt** — full markdown content for AI consumption

**feed.xml** — RSS feed for syndication and aggregators

**ai-plugin.json** — MCP plugin manifest for AI platform discovery

**Per-page .md files** — markdown version of every page at the same URL + .md

robots-strategy.title: Choosing a robots.txt strategy
robots-strategy.body:
The robots.txt strategy controls which AI crawlers can access your site:

**Maximum** (default) — all bots allowed, including training bots. Best for maximum visibility.

**Balanced** — search bots (ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) allowed. Training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) blocked. Your content powers AI answers but isn't used for model training.

**Restrictive** — all AI bots blocked. Only traditional search engines allowed. Not recommended unless legally required.

**Custom** — define your own rules line by line.

backup-schedule.title: Automatic backups
backup-schedule.body:
Set a backup schedule to automatically snapshot all your content, settings, and site config. Backups include everything needed to restore your site to a previous state.

Recommended: **Daily** with 30-day retention. Backups are small (typically under 1 MB) and stored locally. You can also download them as zip files.

deploy-intro.title: Publishing your site
deploy-intro.body:
Deploy builds your site as static HTML and pushes it to a hosting provider. The build pipeline generates all pages, SEO files, RSS feed, and AI discovery files automatically.

Supported providers: **GitHub Pages** (free), **Vercel** (free tier), **Netlify** (free tier), **Fly.io** (EU hosting), **Cloudflare Pages** (fast CDN).

Enable **Auto-deploy on save** to publish automatically every time you save content.

agents-intro.title: What are AI agents?
agents-intro.body:
AI agents generate content based on your brand voice and configuration. Each agent has a role:

**Content Writer** — creates new blog posts, pages, descriptions

**SEO Optimizer** — improves meta fields, keywords, heading structure

**GEO Optimizer** — restructures content for AI citation (answer-first, statistics, sources)

**Translator** — translates content to other languages

**Content Refresher** — updates stale content with current information

Agents produce drafts that land in the **Curation Queue** for your review. They respect **AI Lock** — fields you've edited by hand won't be overwritten.

actions.a0: Review generated content in Curation Queue

media-ai-analysis.title: AI image analysis
media-ai-analysis.body:
AI analysis automatically generates captions, alt text, and tags for your images. Alt text is critical for:

**SEO** — search engines can't see images without alt text

**Accessibility** — screen readers use alt text for visually impaired users

**GEO** — AI platforms use alt text to understand page content

Analysis runs automatically on upload. You can also batch-analyze existing images from the Media library.

media-library-intro.title: Media library
media-library-intro.body:
Upload images, videos, audio, and files. The library auto-generates optimized **WebP variants** and extracts **EXIF metadata** including GPS coordinates.

Organize with **folders** and **user tags**. Search finds files by name, AI caption, alt text, and tags. Drag and drop to upload, or paste from clipboard.

actions.a0: Configure WebP quality and variant sizes

dashboard-intro.title: Your site at a glance
dashboard-intro.body:
The dashboard shows key metrics for your site: content counts per collection, scheduled items, media library size, and SEO health score.

Click any card to jump to that section. The **Visibility score** combines SEO (search engines) and GEO (AI platforms) — aim for 80+.

collection-list-intro.title: Managing documents
collection-list-intro.body:
Each collection holds documents of a type — blog posts, pages, products, etc. Documents have a **status**:

**Published** — live on your site

**Draft** — not visible, work in progress

**Scheduled** — will auto-publish at a set date and time

Use the **Generate** button to create new content with AI, or **New document** for a blank one.

editor-intro.title: Editing content
editor-intro.body:
The editor auto-saves as you type. Use the toolbar for formatting, media, blocks, and tables. Key features:

**AI Lock** — click the lock icon on any field to protect it from AI overwrites

**SEO panel** — click SEO in the toolbar to edit meta title, description, and keywords

**Preview** — click Preview to see the page live on your site

**Cmd+S** — save and sync to disk immediately

actions.a0: Click AI in the toolbar to generate or improve content

curation-intro.title: Review AI-generated content
curation-intro.body:
When AI agents generate content, it lands here for your review before publishing. The curation workflow:

1. **Ready** — content waiting for review
2. **In review** — someone is looking at it
3. **Approved** — ready to publish (click Publish to go live)
4. **Rejected** — needs rework or should be discarded

You can edit content inline before approving. Fields with **AI Lock** were written by a human and won't be touched by agents.

scheduled-intro.title: Content calendar
scheduled-intro.body:
The calendar shows all content with scheduled publish or unpublish dates. The scheduler runs every 60 seconds and automatically changes document status when the time arrives.

To schedule content: open a document, click **Set expiry** or set a publish date in **Properties**, then save.

seo-dashboard-intro.title: SEO dashboard
seo-dashboard-intro.body:
Monitor SEO health across all your content. Each document is scored on 13 rules covering meta fields, content quality, and structured data.

**Optimize All** runs AI optimization on every published document — fills in missing meta titles, descriptions, keywords, and JSON-LD.

**Keyword Tracker** lets you monitor search positions for your target keywords over time.

actions.a0: Click Optimize All to fix all SEO issues at once

linkchecker-intro.title: Finding broken links
linkchecker-intro.body:
The link checker scans all your published content for broken links, redirect chains, and missing pages. It checks both internal links (between your documents) and external links (to other websites).

Broken links hurt SEO and user experience. Run a check after major content updates or before deploying.

performance-intro.title: AI usage analytics
performance-intro.body:
Track AI agent performance across your site: how many documents were generated, how many were accepted vs rejected, token usage, and estimated cost.

Use these metrics to tune your agents — a low acceptance rate means the agent needs better prompts or brand voice training.

backup-intro.title: Backups and restore
backup-intro.body:
Backups snapshot all your content, settings, and site config as a zip file. You can restore to any previous snapshot with one click.

Backups include: all documents, media metadata, site config, agent configs, and deploy settings. Media files themselves are not included (they live in uploads/).

cockpit-intro.title: AI command center
cockpit-intro.body:
The cockpit gives you global control over AI content generation. Adjust:

**Temperature** — higher = more creative, lower = more consistent

**Prompt depth** — how much context the AI receives about your site

**Speed vs quality** — fast drafts or polished output

Changes here affect all AI agents and the chat interface.

interactives-intro.title: Interactive content
interactives-intro.body:
Interactives are data-driven HTML widgets you can embed in any richtext field: calculators, quizzes, comparison tables, timelines. They're stored as standalone HTML documents and rendered in a sandboxed iframe.

Create interactives with AI or write custom HTML/CSS/JS. Embed them in articles using the **Insert interactive** button in the editor toolbar.

trash-intro.title: Trash and recovery
trash-intro.body:
Trashed documents are kept for **30 days** (configurable in Settings) before permanent deletion. You can restore any trashed document to its previous status.

**Purge trash** in Settings → General permanently deletes all trashed documents immediately, regardless of retention period.

settings-team.title: Managing your team
settings-team.body:
Invite team members by email. Each member gets a role:

**Admin** — full access, can manage settings, deploy, and invite others

**Editor** — can create, edit, publish, and trash documents

**Viewer** — read-only access, can preview but not edit

Team members are per-site — different sites can have different teams.

settings-email.title: Transactional email
settings-email.body:
Configure the From address, provider, and notification recipients for outgoing mail.

The CMS sends email for **team invites**, **form submissions**, **agent completion alerts**, **backup failures**, **link-check reports**, and **Lighthouse threshold alerts**.

Without an email provider configured here, invites fall back to showing the signup URL on screen and submissions save to the inbox without notification.

**Provider**: Resend. Paste your API key, pick a verified From domain, send a test to confirm.

actions.a0: Set up a Resend account and domain

settings-geo.title: AI visibility (GEO)
settings-geo.body:
**GEO** (Generative Engine Optimization) controls how AI platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity find and cite your content.

The **robots.txt strategy** is the primary knob:

- **Maximum** — all bots allowed, including training (best for visibility)
- **Balanced** — search bots allowed, training bots blocked
- **Restrictive** — all AI bots blocked
- **Custom** — define your own rules

Each build automatically generates **llms.txt**, **llms-full.txt**, **sitemap.xml**, **robots.txt**, **feed.xml**, and per-page **.md** siblings so AI platforms can discover and cite your content natively.

settings-beam.title: Beam — site export & import
settings-beam.body:
A **beam** is a portable single-file archive of your entire site — content, config, settings, schema, agents, brand voice, team, event log. Use it to migrate between environments or share a site template.

Beams do NOT include uploaded binaries (images, videos) or secrets (API keys are redacted). You re-enter secrets on import.

For scheduled, incremental backups, use Settings → Backup instead.

settings-prompts.title: AI prompt templates
settings-prompts.body:
Override the built-in prompt templates the CMS uses for field generation, SEO optimisation, translation, and every other AI feature — per site.

Each prompt has three parts: **system** (fixed), **user template** (variable with placeholders), **example output** (optional).

Before overriding, try adjusting **Brand Voice** — it's simpler and propagates to every AI feature automatically. Use prompt overrides when you need feature-specific constraints Brand Voice can't express.

settings-general.title: General site settings
settings-general.body:
Basic site identity: **name** (shown in the admin header), **preview URL** (used for previewing pages), **description** (the default meta description), **timezone** (affects schedule and backup times).

The preview URL is how CMS admin builds preview links. Set it to your production URL once deployed, or a localhost dev URL for local preview.

settings-tools.title: Automation settings
settings-tools.body:
Configure automatic tasks that run in the background:

**Link checker schedule** — scan for broken links daily or weekly

**Lighthouse schedule** — performance audits on a cadence

**Media processing** — WebP variant sizes, JPEG quality, EXIF retention

**Webhooks** — outbound HTTP calls when content changes

Each automation runs on the instrumentation-node scheduler and logs to the event log.

settings-globals.title: Global data editing
settings-globals.body:
**Globals** are single-record collections for site-wide data that appears on many pages: footer text, social links, contact details, legal notices.

Each global is edited as one document. Unlike regular collections they don't have `/admin/<collection>/<slug>` URLs — they're edited in this tab and consumed by your site via the content API.

Common globals: `footer`, `legal`, `contact`, `pricing-tiers`. Each gets its own field schema in cms.config.ts.

settings-deploy.title: Deploy targets
settings-deploy.body:
Configure where the Deploy button pushes your built site.

Supported providers: **GitHub Pages** (free), **Vercel** (free tier), **Netlify** (free tier), **Fly.io** (EU regions, Docker-based), **Cloudflare Pages** (fast CDN).

Enable **Deploy on save** to publish automatically after every content change — works with Instant Content Deployment for 2-second pushes on supported frontends.

settings-ai.title: AI model configuration
settings-ai.body:
Configure which AI models power your CMS features:

**Content model** — used for field generation, SEO optimization, translations. Haiku is fast and cheap, Sonnet is balanced.

**Chat model** — used for the Chat interface. Sonnet recommended for best tool-calling.

**Premium model** — used for complex tasks (brand voice, long content). Opus gives highest quality.

**Code model** — used for generating interactives (HTML/CSS/JS).

All models use your Anthropic API key. Token limits control max output per request.

settings-brand-voice.title: Brand voice
settings-brand-voice.body:
Brand voice defines how AI writes for your site. Complete the **brand interview** to teach the AI your tone, audience, and style preferences.

Once configured, all AI-generated content — agents, chat, field generation — follows your brand guidelines. The interview takes 2-3 minutes and dramatically improves output quality.

settings-mcp.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
settings-mcp.body:
MCP lets external AI tools (like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or custom agents) read and write your CMS content via a standard protocol.

**Authenticated MCP** — full read/write access with API key. Use for content production.

**Public MCP** — read-only, no auth needed. Use for AI-powered search on your site.

Copy the MCP config JSON and paste it into your AI tool's settings.

settings-deploy-icd.title: Instant Content Deployment
settings-deploy-icd.body:
For Next.js sites on Fly.io, content changes are pushed directly via webhook in **~2 seconds** — no Docker rebuild needed. This is called **Instant Content Deployment (ICD)**.

When ICD is configured (revalidateUrl + secret), saving content triggers a signed webhook that writes the document to the deployed site and revalidates the page. Full deploys are only needed for code changes.

settings-schema.title: Editing collection schemas
settings-schema.body:
Schemas define the fields available in each collection. Add, remove, or reorder fields here. Changes take effect immediately — no restart needed.

**Field types**: text, textarea, richtext, number, boolean, date, image, image-gallery, video, audio, file, select, tags, relation, array, object, blocks, map, interactive, column-slots.

Be careful removing fields — existing content using those fields will keep the data but it won't be visible in the editor.

lighthouse-intro.title: Lighthouse performance audit
lighthouse-intro.body:
Lighthouse scans your deployed site via Google PageSpeed Insights and scores it on four categories: **Performance**, **Accessibility**, **SEO**, and **Best Practices**.

Scores use Google's thresholds: 🟢 90-100 (good), 🟡 50-89 (needs work), 🔴 0-49 (poor).

**Core Web Vitals** are the metrics Google uses for search ranking:
- **LCP** — main content load time (target: < 2.5s)
- **CLS** — layout shift during load (target: < 0.1)
- **FCP** — first text/image visible (target: < 1.8s)
- **TTFB** — server response time (target: < 800ms)

**Opportunities** show specific improvements with estimated savings. **Diagnostics** flag issues like large DOM, unused JavaScript, or missing cache headers.

Each scan runs **both mobile and desktop** in parallel and displays results side by side. Scans require a publicly accessible URL — set your production URL as the site's Preview URL in Settings.
